Computational domains

Source: R/domain.R
pde_domain.Rd

pde_domain() describes the geometry on which a PDE is posed. Domains are pure geometric descriptions; a mesh is built from a domain with pde_mesh_rectangle() or pde_mesh_polygon(). One-dimensional and three-dimensional domains are planned but not yet available.

Usage

pde_domain(
  type = c("rectangle", "polygon"),
  x = c(0, 1),
  y = c(0, 1),
  vertices = NULL,
  markers = "boundary",
  holes = NULL,
  hole_markers = "hole"
)

Arguments

type

One of "rectangle" or "polygon".

x

For rectangles, the two endpoints in the x direction.

y

For rectangles, the two endpoints in the y direction.

vertices

For polygons, a two-column numeric matrix of vertices.

markers

For polygons, a character vector naming each side, or a single name used for every side.

holes

For polygons, an optional list of vertex matrices, each a simple polygon strictly inside the outer polygon; holes must not touch each other or the outer boundary.

hole_markers

Marker of the sides of each hole: one name for all holes or one per hole.

Value

An object of class pde_domain.

Details

Supported types:

  • "rectangle": the open rectangle (x[1], x[2]) x (y[1], y[2]). Boundary markers are "bottom", "right", "top" and "left".

  • "polygon": a simple polygon given by its vertices in order. Side i joins vertex i to vertex i + 1 (and the last vertex to the first). markers names each side; by default all sides are "boundary".

Every domain also answers to the marker "boundary", which selects the whole boundary.

Validation rejects non-finite coordinates, zero-length sides, repeated vertices, zero area and self-intersecting polygons. A clockwise polygon is reversed to counterclockwise order (its side markers are reversed with it) and a message reports the change.

Examples

pde_domain("rectangle", x = c(0, 1), y = c(0, 2))
#> <pde_domain> rectangle 
#>   (0, 1) x (0, 2)
#>   markers: bottom, right, top, left 
L <- rbind(c(0, 0), c(2, 0), c(2, 1), c(1, 1), c(1, 2), c(0, 2))
pde_domain("polygon", vertices = L)
#> <pde_domain> polygon 
#>   vertices: 6 
#>   markers: boundary
